steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Spray 9-inch glass pie pan with cooking spray.
Cook beef and onion in a nonstick skillet over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until beef is browned and crumbly, 8 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk milk, Bisquick, and eggs together in a small bowl.
Drain beef and onion mixture; transfer to the prepared pie pan. Stir in salt, sprinkle with Cheddar, and pour Bisquick mixture over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Impossibly Easy Cheeseburger Pie
raw_recipe.description: Enjoy this savory dinner pie with juicy ground beef, biscuit mix, and Cheddar cheese. It tastes just like a cheeseburger but you eat it with a fork!
raw_recipe.name: Impossibly Easy Cheeseburger Pie

review.reviewBody: Haha. Some really hated this recipe. Some thought it was 'bland'. Well, duh. If you treat this as more than a concept recipe, you are probably going to be disappointed. After all, who eats PLAIN cheeseburgers? (My little cousin, but that's besides the point.) I dressed this as I would my regular burgers. Layers were: hamburger (seasoned with garlic and onion powder), crumbled bacon, raw onions (mm, crunchy), chopped dill pickles (trust me), cheese, homemade buttermilk biscuit (dough that I had in the fridge). When it was cooked, I plated it on top of whole leaf lettuce, would have added tomatoes if I had 'em, and thousand island dressing. It was tasty, casserole-y, and cheeseburger-y. Get out there and experiment. Recipes are not set in stone. (Unless it is creme brulee, I'm pretty sure that's set in stone somewhere... in France.) Thanks for a good start to a decent supper.

I forgot the first rule of recipe tryout: Read reviews first! I made this exactly as written except I added a couple of minced garlic cloves. I should have used a little salt, although I don't salt anything any more. I whisked the Bisquick with milk & eggs & it was very runny. Finished dish was a little bland, improved with ketchup &, while the Bisquick did creep into all the nooks & crannies, it tasted under-cooked. The second time I made this I cut the milk to 1/3 C. & added 3 eggs. I also placed 1/2 ground beef in pie pan, added the cheese then remaining meat. Baked it for 20 minutes, added more cheese to the top & returned it to oven to finish. I also added salt this time. Perfection! This is now in my permanent rotation of meals.

This recipe didn't use the 1/4 cup of ketchup to be added to the onion and ground meat at the end for just a few mins then put in the pie plate then the Bisquick mixture The ketchup makes a big difference

I followed others suggestions and gave this recipe some punch. I browned the meat with the onion and chopped garlic. I then added chopped pickles, ketchup, mustard, Worcestershire, hamburger seasoning and then the cheese. I poured this into the pie pan and topped it with the Bisquick mix with 1/2 cup of milk and 3 eggs. It turned out GREAT. I'll be making this often.

I have made this twice. The first time my husband and I both thought it was rather bland. Last night I made it again. I added extra onion, garlic and sautéed fresh tomatoes, fresh from the garden. I also added pepper and a couple of shots of tabasco sauce. It turned out flavorful and delicious. This is an easy recipe and by adding some extras you can adjust it to make it your own! Will be making this for our churches drive through meal giveaway in a couple of weeks (for 100 people!).
I sauteed onions in butter, added garlic and Worcestershire sauce to meat. Used double recipe. Turned out great

Like everyone else, I read the reviews and changed it up. I’m not a big fan of Bisquick, so I used a box of Cheddar Bay Biscuit mix instead. With 2 eggs I figured it would puff up a lot, so I didn’t use quite the whole bag of the mix. I just kept adding little bits more until the batter seemed right for this kind of use (the dough for these can be thick and sticky). Then I added the whole flavor packet and a bit more salt and garlic powder. I put the pie together and baked as the recipe directed, then piled more cheddar cheese on top and cooked for another 4 minutes to melt. I let it stand 10 minutes before serving. Yum! Where has this been all my life?!

I made this exactly as written except I added 2 dashes of Tabasco and one minced garlic clove to the meat and onion mixture while it cooked. As I used very lean beef, there was nothing really to drain off so I skipped that part.

I used to make this when our boys were still at home. I was always looking for ways to get vegetables into every meal, so with this I just added about 3/4 cup frozen mixed vegetables (thawed) with the beef. And I added about 1/2 cup of mild or medium salsa, some garlic powder (around 1 teaspoon but more or less for preferences), and about 1/2 cup chopped onion, browned along with the ground beef. I usually add 1 teaspoon chili powder too. So this is how I jazzed it up to make it a little more nutritious and interesting. We all really like it that way. Now that it's just two of us, I cut the recipe in half and bake it in a 1 quart round baking dish. That makes about 3 servings so someone has some leftover for a lunch or late night snack. It reheats well in the microwave.

This is very easy and delicious after I doctored it up. There wasn't any seasoning other than a little salt so I knew if I didn't do something it wouldn't taste like anything let alone a cheeseburger. So I added garlic powder, onion powder, ground mustard, pepper, and ketchup. Served it with fried pickles and salad.

On yeah! I shook in some garlic powder, added a dash of Worcestershire, and the kids loved it! Then I made another , starting with about a quarter pound smoked salmon with pepper. Then I sauteed a red pepper with a quarter pound of baby spinach. I layered in those veg with half cup of loosely packed green onion. I used southwestern style egg beaters and whole milk and it was AWESOME!!! I used sharp cheddar on both. And Jiffy baking mix. For another option, fill the pie pan with raw broccoli, then microwave the broccoli and proceed! I also put bacon bits in that one.
Good week night recipe although I would add additional seasoning to the meat mixture while cooking next time. Perhaps some garlic powder and worchester sause.
My kids said not to make this one again.
I followed the recipe as written and my family LOVES it. We've made it so many times.
Instead of hamburger I use deer meat
I added spinach to my recipe for added iron, and my husband raved about it for 3 days!

Yes it is kind of bland, but that is because this is a base recipe that is very versatile. Any ground or shredded meat will work, any melting cheese will work, experiment with spices if you want. just a few ideas, some I've tried, some I've never had a chance to. add ins I've tried that were good- mushrooms, peppers bell peppers or hot peppers, dill relish. Pizza Pie- Shredded Italian blend cheese, ground sausage and any other pizza topping (I would suggest chopping pepperoni so that batter seeps around it correctly) Taco Pie-add taco seasoning o ground beef, add black beans, peppers, mexican cheese. Breakfast Pie-Ground sausage, hashbrown potatoes, you can even omit the bisquick, and pour thin pancake batter. it's only as bland or as spicy as you make it.
Do yourself a favor: mix the Bisquick with the eggs first, and THEN mix in the milk. You can thank me later lol.
Added pickled. Needs bacon for a little more flavor. I might even try a spoon of dijon mustard next time.
My granddaughter loves this!
